_**Agent (default)**_

No. This workflow is **not** wired to `push`.

It only runs on **`pull_request`** when the PR targets **`main`** (for example when you open or update a PR into `main`). Pushes that are not part of a PR to `main` (e.g. direct pushes to `main` or pushes on branches with no PR) will not start this workflow unless you add a `push:` trigger.

will it run on a draft PR?

---

_**Agent (default)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Checking GitHub Actions behavior**

I'm verifying GitHub Actions behavior for draft PRs using `pull_request` triggers. </details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Yes. With only this:

```2:5:/Users/ronessaacquesta/activiqhq/.github/workflows/run-unit-test.yml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
```

GitHub uses the default `pull_request` activity types (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`). **Draft PRs still get those events** when they’re opened or when you push new commits, so this workflow **will run on draft PRs** the same as non-draft ones.

To skip drafts you’d add something like a job-level condition: `if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false`, or narrow `pull_request` `types` (that alone usually isn’t enough to exclude drafts—you still need the `draft` check).

_**Agent (default)**_

Identifying two likely causes:

1. Marking ready for review — Default `pull_request` types are only `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened`. Converting draft → ready emits `ready_for_review`, which isn't included, so no run unless we push (synchronize).

2. Workflow missing on the PR branch — GitHub runs the workflow from the PR's head branch. If the branch was created before `run-unit-test.yml` existed and wasn't updated, the workflow may not run on open.

Adding `ready_for_review` to the workflow triggers so marking a PR ready runs CI.

Here is what was going on and what we changed.

### Why “Ready for review” did nothingWith `pull_request` and **no** `types`, GitHub only runs the workflow for **`opened`**, **`synchronize`** (new commits on the branch), and **`reopened`**. Turning a draft into a normal PR fires **`ready_for_review`**, which was **not** in that set, so CI did not start unless you pushed again.

`types` was added so **`ready_for_review`** is included; marking the PR ready will trigger a run like a new push.

### Why opening the draft might not have run
- **Head branch must contain this workflow.** Runs use the workflow file from the **PR branch**. If that branch was cut before `run-unit-test.yml` existed and never got those commits, Actions may not run until you merge/rebase **`main`** into the branch (or recreate the branch from current `main`).
- **PR base must be `main`.** Your filter is `branches: [main]` (the **base** branch). Your remote default is `main`, so that matches your setup; if you ever target another base, this workflow will not run.
- **Fork PRs:** first-time contributors often need a maintainer to **approve workflow runs** before any job starts.

After pulling the updated workflow into your PR branch, you should see a run when you open/update the PR and when you click **Ready for review**. If opening a new draft still shows nothing, check the PR’s **Files changed** tab for `.github/workflows/run-unit-test.yml` on that branch and the **Actions** tab for “Workflow run pending approval.”
